counterparty.name: SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX

missingRules.expectedFix: Add Licensor defense and indemnity for third-party IP claims, legal violations, Vendor-caused data breaches, and gross negligence or willful misconduct, with standard procedures and remedies.
missingRules.note: No Vendor indemnity exists; Article XII instead imposes a broad one-way indemnity on Licensee for use of Licensor's technology and services.

missingRules.expectedFix: Require CGL, E&O, cyber/privacy, and workers' compensation coverage at the playbook limits, with certificates available on request.
missingRules.note: The Agreement contains no obligation for Licensor to maintain vendor insurance.

missingRules.expectedFix: Require post-termination assistance, machine-readable return of Licensee data within 30 days, and certified deletion after transition.
missingRules.note: There is no Licensor transition assistance, Licensee data export, or deletion certification; only Licensee must return Licensor materials.

missingRules.expectedFix: Allow Licensee to terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
missingRules.note: Licensee has no usable termination-for-convenience right during the 36-month initial term or possible seven-year renewal.

missingRules.expectedFix: Add professional-and-workmanlike services and software conformance warranties with repair, replacement, or refund remedies, applicable warranty periods, legal compliance, and no-malicious-code protection.
missingRules.note: The Licensed Technology is expressly provided AS IS and all express and implied warranties are disclaimed, leaving no usable performance warranty.

spans.expectedFix: Delete the unilateral seven-year option and require mutual written agreement, or use 12-month renewals with Licensee able to opt out on no more than 60 days' notice.
spans.note: Licensor has a unilateral option to impose a seven-year renewal, contrary to the mutual-extension language elsewhere and the prohibition on automatic multi-year renewals.

spans.expectedFix: No change is needed because New York law and exclusive New York City jurisdiction are preferred.
spans.note: New York law and the associated exclusive New York City courts match the preferred governing-law and venue position.

spans.expectedFix: Delete the restriction or make it mutual, limited to directly involved personnel for 12 months, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach exceptions.
spans.note: The Licensee-only non-solicit covers all Licensor and affiliate employees for three years after termination, exceeding the 24-month walkaway threshold.

spans.expectedFix: Permit Licensee change-of-control transactions without consent and remove Licensor's subjective withholding and termination rights.
spans.note: Licensor may withhold change-of-control consent based on broad competitive or subjective adverse-interest grounds.

spans.expectedFix: Allow assignment in a merger, acquisition, change of control, or sale of substantially all assets without Licensor consent or automatic termination.
spans.note: Licensee's agreement and licenses automatically terminate upon a change of control unless Licensor gives prior written consent.

spans.expectedFix: Permit assignments to affiliates and M&A successors without consent, with consent not unreasonably withheld for other assignments.
spans.note: The clause voids all Licensee assignments and license transfers without consent and provides no affiliate or M&A carve-out.

spans.expectedFix: Add express transfer rights for affiliates and M&A successors and permitted use by contractors acting for Licensee.
spans.note: Licensee cannot transfer any interest in the Licensed Technology under any circumstances without Licensor consent, including to successors.

spans.expectedFix: Permit assignment to affiliates and successors in merger, acquisition, or asset-sale transactions without consent.
spans.note: Licensee is subject to a blanket consent requirement for assignment or transfer, without an affiliate or M&A exception.

spans.expectedFix: Permit transfer to M&A successors and access by authorized affiliates and contractors acting on Licensee's behalf.
spans.note: The licensed programs cannot be assigned or transferred to any third party without specific approval, with no successor or contractor path.

spans.expectedFix: Extend the license to affiliates and contractors acting for Licensee, make it transferable to M&A successors, and prohibit discretionary revocation.
spans.note: The license is narrowly limited to Licensee and the Field of Use, with no coverage for affiliates, contractors, or successors.

spans.expectedFix: No change is needed because a non-exclusive license and Licensor's continued ownership and licensing rights are acceptable.
spans.note: The license's non-exclusive status and Licensor's reservation of rights do not improperly restrict Licensee under the playbook.

spans.expectedFix: Limit audits to once per 12 months on at least 30 days' written notice during normal business hours.
spans.note: The clause requires an audit within 30 days after a request but sets neither minimum advance notice nor an annual frequency limit.

spans.expectedFix: Provide that Licensor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes a Licensee underpayment exceeding 5%.
spans.note: Licensee must pay audit costs for any discrepancy over 5%, rather than only for an established underpayment over 5%.

spans.expectedFix: Require auditor confidentiality, limit review to relevant accounting records, prohibit direct system access, and confine audits to verifying amounts due.
spans.note: Although the auditor is independent and mutually selected, the clause lacks confidentiality protections and clear limits on audit scope and system access.

spans.expectedFix: Replace this with mutual caps and indirect-damages exclusions, subject to uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, security, indemnity, IP infringement, gross negligence, willful misconduct, and fraud.
spans.note: Licensor disclaims nearly all liability except direct damages from gross negligence or willful misconduct, while Licensee receives no reciprocal protection.

spans.expectedFix: Make the exclusion mutual and add carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnification, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, and IP infringement.
spans.note: The consequential-damages exclusion protects only Licensor and lacks required carve-outs, including for data loss, indemnity, and IP infringement.

spans.expectedFix: Use a mutual cap equal to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and $1,000,000, with the required uncapped carve-outs or indemnity super-cap.
spans.note: Only Licensor is capped, at one-half of amounts already paid, while Licensee's liability and one-way indemnity remain uncapped.

spans.expectedFix: No change is needed because the exclusion is mutual and limited to a contractually proper termination or expiration.
spans.note: This mutual exclusion applies only to damages arising from termination or expiration carried out in accordance with the Agreement.

spans.expectedFix: Delete the blanket disclaimer and subject service failures to the mutual liability cap, express warranties, and required liability carve-outs.
spans.note: Licensor disclaims all liability for core delivery, operation, availability, performance, and termination failures without meaningful exceptions.
